test_cases.question: What must a court do when it learns about similar GDPR proceedings in another Member State?
test_cases.answer: Where a competent court of a Member State has information on proceedings, concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor, that are pending in a court in another Member State, it shall contact that court in the other Member State to confirm the existence of such proceedings.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where a competent court of a Member State has information on proceedings, concerning the same subject matter as regards processing by the same controller or processor, that are pending in a court in another Member State, it shall contact that court in the other Member State to confirm the existence of such proceedings

test_cases.question: When can a court suspend its proceedings in a GDPR case?
test_cases.answer: Where proceedings concerning the same subject matter as regards processing of the same controller or processor are pending in a court in another Member State, any competent court other than the court first seized may suspend its proceedings. The court first seized retains priority.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where proceedings concerning the same subject matter as regards processing of the same controller or processor are pending in a court in another Member State, any competent court other than the court first seized may suspend its proceedings
key_phrases: pending in a court in another Member State

test_cases.question: Under what conditions can a court decline jurisdiction in favor of another court?
test_cases.answer: A court may decline jurisdiction only when: (1) the proceedings are pending at first instance; (2) the request is made on the application of one of the parties; (3) the court is not the court first seized; (4) the court first seized has jurisdiction over the actions in question; and (5) the law of the court first seized permits the consolidation of the actions.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where those proceedings are pending at first instance, any court other than the court first seized may also, on the application of one of the parties, decline jurisdiction if the court first seized has jurisdiction over the actions in question and its law permits the consolidation thereof
key_phrases: application of one of the parties

test_cases.question: Does the duty to contact another court about parallel proceedings apply when both sets of proceedings are pending within the same Member State?
test_cases.answer: No. Article 81 applies only when proceedings are pending in a court in another Member State. Coordination of parallel cases within the same country is governed by that Member State's domestic procedural law, not GDPR Article 81.
test_cases.supporting_quote: pending in a court in another Member State

b2b_relevance: MEDIUM - Article 81 prevents conflicting judgments when you face GDPR lawsuits in multiple EU countries. Key points: (1) If sued in multiple MS for same processing, courts must coordinate, (2) 'Court first seized' has priority, (3) Later courts may suspend or decline, (4) This provides some protection against forum shopping abuse. Strategically, filing first may establish favorable jurisdiction.
